module_summary: Release-kit inputs and the first slice of the host test suite. ship/ holds the RiptOPL pin list that scripts/package_kit.py refreshes and checks, the AFL licence copied into the kit, and five .url shortcuts the packer validates; all are used. The tests are standalone Python scripts run one by one from .github/workflows/compile.yml (lines 50-266): most cut production C functions out of src/ with a brace-matching extractor, wrap them in hand-written stubs, compile with host gcc/clang and run; a few are pure text checks of sources, scripts or docs. The *_host.c files are C drivers for the memory-card modules (mc_card_view/write, mc_ps1_card, mc_save_formats/export, mmce_save_versions, dash_card_tool) and mc_fixture.py builds PS2 card images for them; test_cf.c/test_cis.c are compiled by tests/test_pccf.py and pccf_ata_card.h by tests/test_pccf_ata.c. test_dash_card_tool.py is the largest and slowest (its own comment estimates ~700 MB of card images per run).

reusable_helpers.name: Card
reusable_helpers.what: builds a formatted PS2 memory-card image in memory (directories, files, icon.sys, optional ECC) for host tests

reusable_helpers.name: standard_card
reusable_helpers.what: returns a ready-made card image with the standard set of test saves

reusable_helpers.name: icon_sys
reusable_helpers.what: builds an icon.sys block from an SJIS title and line-break offset

reusable_helpers.name: slurp
reusable_helpers.what: reads a whole file into a malloc'd buffer (exits on error); copied in mc_save_export_host.c and mc_save_formats_host.c

reusable_helpers.name: spit
reusable_helpers.what: writes a whole buffer to a file (exits on error); copied in mc_save_export_host.c

reusable_helpers.name: rd
reusable_helpers.what: McViewSource read callback over a FILE*; copied in mc_card_write_host.c and mc_fingerprint_host.c

reusable_helpers.name: function
reusable_helpers.what: string- and char-literal-aware brace matcher that cuts one C function out of a source file

reusable_helpers.name: genOpen/genDopen/fileXioDread POSIX stand-ins
reusable_helpers.what: POSIX implementations of the dashboard gen* file API with one-open-file check and fault injection

findings.title: tests/test_boot_deferred_init.py is never run: not listed in compile.yml, and it only searches dash_main.c text
findings.problem: compile.yml runs each test by name (lines 50-266) and test_boot_deferred_init.py is not among them; the only other mention of the file in the repo is a comment in test_dashboard_console_summary.py:36. The file itself compiles nothing: every check is a substring or regex over src/dash_main.c (lines 24-47), so it guards spelling, not behaviour, and nobody runs it.
findings.fix: Delete tests/test_boot_deferred_init.py and drop the pointer to it from the comment at tests/test_dashboard_console_summary.py:36.
findings.benefit: 49 lines removed (whole file) and one stale cross-reference; no CI change because it never ran (MEASURED: grep of compile.yml).
findings.evidence: Grep 'tests/test_[a-z0-9_]+.py' in .github/workflows/compile.yml lists 214 test runs at lines 52-265 and 449; test_boot_deferred_init is absent. Grep 'test_boot_deferred_init|boot_deferred' over src/Launchstation: only tests/test_dashboard_console_summary.py:36 (comment). Read test_boot_deferred_init.py 1-49: function() extractor, then assert/regex on main text only.

findings.title: Brace-matching C function extractor copy-pasted into 110 test files (16 in this unit, three string-aware variants)
findings.problem: Each test defines its own function()/extract()/fn() that finds a signature and counts braces to the matching close; Grep finds a top-level definition in 110 files under tests/. The bodies are the same algorithm with cosmetic differences, and three files (cloud_history_browser, cloud_recovery, cloud_upload_ledger) carry a 26-30 line string/char-literal-aware version that the others lack, so a brace inside a string literal breaks some tests and not others.
findings.fix: Put one extractor (the string-aware one from test_cloud_history_browser.py) in a small tests/csource.py and import it, as tests already import mc_fixture via sys.path.insert(0, Path(__file__).parent); delete the local copies.
findings.justification: Adds one ~30-line module; removes 182 lines in the cited ranges of this unit alone and roughly 8 lines in each of ~94 further files, and gives every test the same literal-aware parsing.
findings.benefit: ~150 net lines removed in this unit (182 cited minus ~30 for the shared module), MEASURED from ranges; ~750 more repo-wide (110 files x ~8 lines), INFERRED.
findings.evidence: Grep '^def (function|extract|fn|func|body|c_function)\(' in tests/: 110 files, one each. Read all 16 in this unit plus test_launch_driver_messages.py:27-34. String-aware variants: cloud_history_browser 17-46, cloud_recovery 19-46, cloud_upload_ledger 19-44. Shared import precedent: sys.path.insert in test_dash_card_tool.py:19, test_mc_card_write.py:22, test_mc_fingerprint.py:19, test_mc_card_view.py:9, test_mmce_save_versions.py:17, test_mmce_fingerprint_backup.py:16.

findings.title: Tests assert that compile.yml runs themselves, which cannot fail in CI
findings.problem: Each line asserts that the string 'python3 tests/<this file>.py' appears in compile.yml. When CI runs the test the line is necessarily there, so the assert can only fire when a developer runs the file by hand after deleting it from the workflow. In test_cloud_upload_ledger.py and test_dash_card_tool.py the workflow text is read only for this assert.
findings.fix: Delete the self-referencing asserts, and the compile.yml read in the two files where nothing else uses it.
findings.benefit: ~11 lines removed and one file read per run (MEASURED: 9 assert lines plus 2 read lines in the two unit files).
findings.evidence: Grep 'in workflow' over the listed test files gives exactly these self-name asserts. Grep 'workflow' in test_cloud_upload_ledger.py: lines 15-16 only; in test_dash_card_tool.py: lines 23-24 only. test_dash_pause.py:22 reads and asserts in one line. Other files' workflow variable may have further uses, so only the assert line is cited there.

findings.title: Asserts that long-removed helper names stay absent (test_copy_pipeline.py, test_copy_short_io.py)
findings.problem: test_copy_pipeline.py checks that copyPrepareTarget, copyLookupPath, copyVerifyTarget, copyPublishTarget, copyOpenTarget and three strings are not in filer_copy.c; test_copy_short_io.py checks the same for copyReadChunk/copyWriteChunk. None of these names exists anywhere else in the repo, so the checks only guard against re-adding a name; they test code that no longer exists and say nothing about behaviour, which the rest of both files already exercises.
findings.fix: Delete the three lines in test_copy_pipeline.py and line 54 in test_copy_short_io.py.
findings.benefit: 4 lines removed (MEASURED from ranges); no coverage lost because the compiled harnesses in both files test the current copy path.
findings.evidence: Grep 'copyPrepareTarget|copyLookupPath|copyVerifyTarget|copyPublishTarget|copyOpenTarget|copyReadChunk|copyWriteChunk' over src/Launchstation: only test_copy_short_io.py:54 and test_copy_pipeline.py:18-19.

findings.title: Source-text-only checks: test_cloud_relay.py as a whole, plus substring-assert blocks inside behavioural tests
findings.problem: test_cloud_relay.py (run at compile.yml:186) only checks that the relay .ps1, .bat and README contain or lack strings; nothing executes. The listed blocks in otherwise behavioural tests pin exact source spellings (e.g. a whitespace-exact two-line string at test_cloud_upload_ledger.py:52-53, 'genRemove not in body' at test_cloud_history_browser.py:61-64, a licence header and ps2.yaml line at test_cloud_link_screen.py:18-19). They fail on harmless reformatting and pass on broken behaviour; test_cloud_recovery.py:62 is an 'X not in s or Y not in s' check that passes if either string is absent.
findings.fix: Delete test_cloud_relay.py and its compile.yml line. In the listed blocks delete the substring asserts that restate code already compiled and run by the same file; keep only those that pin a wiring point the harness cannot reach, and say which bug each guards in a comment.
findings.benefit: 27 lines (cloud_relay + workflow line) MEASURED; ~50 more assert lines across the blocks INFERRED (blocks total ~80 lines, not all removable); fewer false failures on reformatting.
findings.evidence: Read test_cloud_relay.py 1-26: three read_text calls and asserts only. compile.yml:186 runs it. Re-read test_cloud_history_browser 49-64, test_cloud_recovery 49-62, test_cloud_upload_ledger 50-62, test_cloud_link_screen 18-19 and 60-69, test_dash_card_tool 1215-1217, 1408, 1411-1412: all `in`/`not in`/index-order checks on source text. Other ranges read before notes were compacted.

findings.title: test_cloud_tls_paths.py lines 22-65 test the host compiler's -ffile-prefix-map, not scripts/build_cloud_tls.sh
findings.problem: After checking the script text (16-20), the test writes its own one-line C file, compiles it with and without -ffile-prefix-map and compares objects; the shell escaping it exercises at line 59 is a Python re-implementation, not the script's. It therefore proves that gcc/clang implement the flag, which is toolchain behaviour, while the repo's own wiring is covered only by the text checks above it. The docstring itself calls it 'a portable host compiler smoke test, not a PS2 ELF reproducibility proof'.
findings.fix: Delete lines 22-65 and keep the text checks at 16-20 (or delete the file if those are judged not worth a CI step).
findings.benefit: 44 lines removed and four host compiles per CI run (MEASURED: 2x2 compiles at 36-40 plus one at 60-63).
findings.evidence: Read test_cloud_tls_paths.py 1-67. Source text compiled: line 32 and 57 (test-written). Escaping: line 59 str.replace in Python. build_cloud_tls.sh is only read at line 13 and used in 16-20. compile.yml:240 runs the file.

findings.title: Same file and POSIX helpers repeated across the C host harnesses (rd x3, slurp x3, spit x2, gen* stand-ins x2)
findings.problem: rd() is byte-identical in three harnesses; slurp()/spit() are identical in mc_ps1_card_host.c and mc_save_export_host.c, with a NULL-returning slurp variant in mc_save_formats_host.c; genLseek/genRead, genClose, genDclose/fileXioDread and genCmpFileExt are the same in dash_card_tool_host.c and mmce_save_versions_host.c (fileXioDread differs only in hisize). The path-mapping and fault-injection stand-ins differ and are not part of this finding.
findings.fix: Move rd, slurp, spit and the identical gen* stand-ins into one static-inline header in tests/ (for example host_io.h) included by these harnesses, and delete the copies.
findings.justification: Adds one header of ~60 lines; removes ~115 duplicated lines, so the harnesses cannot drift (mc_save_formats already behaves differently on read errors).
findings.benefit: ~55 net lines removed (MEASURED: 24 rd + 72 slurp/spit + ~35 gen* duplicated lines, minus ~60 for the header, rounded); no product change.
findings.evidence: Read all cited ranges side by side. Grep 'static .*(rd|slurp|spit)\(' in tests/: the six host files plus an unrelated slurp in test_app_packages.py:56. Script lead: mc_ps1_card_host.c 16% same as mc_save_export_host.c; mmce_save_versions_host.c 19% same as dash_card_tool_host.c.

findings.title: test_copy_pipeline.py and test_copy_psu_listing.py repeat the same ~40-line C define/typedef prefix and ~20 stubs
findings.problem: Both harnesses for src/filer_copy.c open with the same typedefs and #defines (MAX_PATH through DPRINTF: PM_*, TRANSFER_*, MC_ATTR_*, FIO_*), differing only in DVRP and the FIO_S_ISDIR/ISREG forms, and repeat stubs such as Timer, getIopResetGeneration, waitUntilTimer, drawMsg, readpad, DashIsActive, nonDialog, isPcCardCfPath/Online, ensureMemoryCardPortAccessible, makeHostPath, filerDirReadComplete, genFixPath and genGetStat. test_copy_psu_listing.py:170 even says 'As in test_copy_pipeline.py'. A new constant used by filer_copy.c has to be added to both.
findings.fix: Move the common defines and the identical stubs into one C fragment (a tests/ header or a Python string in a shared module) that both harness strings start with; keep the per-test stubs local.
findings.justification: Adds one shared fragment of about the size of one copy; removes the second copy and the need to edit two files when filer_copy.c gains a dependency.
findings.benefit: ~45 lines removed (MEASURED: ~42 matching define/typedef lines plus ~15 identical one-line stubs, minus include/import lines); INFERRED less churn on filer_copy.c changes.
findings.evidence: Read test_copy_pipeline.py 14-138 and test_copy_psu_listing.py 55-189 side by side. Defines 42-83 match 58-102 except DVRP (psu_listing 65) and FIO_S_IS* (pipeline 76-77 vs psu_listing 93-96). Identical stubs e.g. pipeline 109/110/115/116/118/119/124/126-129/133-135 vs psu_listing 144/145/149/150/153/154/157/161-164/182-184. sceMcTblGetDir/FILEINFO/iox_stat_t layouts differ and stay local.

findings.title: Dead or redundant test code: unused failedSaves stub and its flag, unused _whole, repeated dash_browser.c reads and F/G reassignments
findings.problem: test_clock_save_action.py stubs failedSaves() (marked unused) but the extracted settingsSaveSoftwareClock (dash_settings.c:2526) calls dashStoreSettingsFailed(), not failedSaves(), so setting unrelated_failed at line 59 changes nothing and the check at 60 does not test what it suggests. In test_dash_card_tool.py, _whole (275) is never read yet runs the saves() helper twice; 433 and 1411 re-read src/dash_browser.c into _br although line 25 already holds it in browser; 449 and 458 reassign F and G to the values set at 280 and 287.
findings.fix: Delete test_clock_save_action.py:34 and the unrelated_failed flag (26, 59); delete test_dash_card_tool.py:275, 449 and 458, and use browser instead of _br at 433-436 and 1411-1412.
findings.benefit: ~6 lines removed and two subprocess runs of the card lister per test run (MEASURED: line 275 calls saves(B) twice).
findings.evidence: Grep 'failedSaves' over repo: stub at test_clock_save_action.py:34; dash_settings.c defines it at 2432 and calls it at 2520/3685/3929, none inside settingsSaveSoftwareClock (2526-); that function calls dashStoreSettingsFailed at 2535. Grep '_whole|_br|^F =|^G =|dash_browser.c' in test_dash_card_tool.py: _whole only at 275; browser read at 25, _br at 433 and 1411; F at 280/449 and G at 287/458 with identical values.

findings.title: Optional git-ref argv mode in test_copy_short_io.py and test_cursor_sound_ticks.py that CI never uses
findings.problem: These tests read sources through 'git show <argv[1]>:path' when given an argument, a bisect aid. compile.yml runs them with no argument (lines 67, 228, 227) and no doc mentions passing a ref to them (the only documented use of the pattern is for test_device_input.py in USB-STABILITY-AUDIT-2026-10-08.md:95). In test_copy_short_io.py the mode also silently skips the seek checks at 95-98.
findings.fix: Delete the argv branch and read the working-tree file directly; git worktree or checkout already gives the same bisect ability.
findings.benefit: ~8 lines removed across three files and one less code path per test (MEASURED from ranges).
findings.evidence: Grep "git', 'show'|\"git\", \"show\"" in tests/: argv mode in test_copy_short_io:13, test_cursor_sound_ticks:22, test_launch_driver_messages:23 (plus test_device_input, test_home_focus, test_modal_animation, test_settings_save_prompt outside this unit). compile.yml lines 67, 227, 228 pass no argument. Grep for documented ref use in md/yml/html/sh/ps1: only USB-STABILITY-AUDIT-2026-10-08.md:95 (test_device_input).
